episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: For two weeks this beat has been about the supply side of offensive-cyber capability in AI models — who gets to buy it, at what tier, from which country. Today, for the first time, a lab published what happened on the other side of the counter.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: We recorded Friday's briefing before the August consumer price print and refused to guess at it. It landed a few hours later, and it landed hot on the one leg that actually matters. Core consumer prices rose three tenths of a percent in August, a tenth of a point above most estimates, after two tenths in July.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: For four straight sessions this show has tracked how the AI infrastructure boom gets financed. Warrants, vendor guarantees, a twenty billion dollar Oracle stock sale. Every time, the instrument stayed on the cap table. Today that pattern breaks, and it breaks into the public bond market.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: For the past week this beat has been arguing about what a model costs. This week the more interesting question changed. Not what a model costs, but what an agent is allowed to do with your money.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday this beat's running complaint was that the week's biggest numbers had no price attached to them. Today two of them got prices. Neither price is reassuring.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: For five straight sessions this beat has kept returning to the same question. Where is the one number in physical AI that somebody other than the vendor has to stand behind? This week we got it, and it is unflattering.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: This sector is usually graded on what operators promise. Launch cadence, deployment counts, revenue guidance. Today we can do something rarer. The proliferated missile-warning layer finally has a price per satellite attached to it, and it falls out of a contract split that has only now become visible.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Two numbers came out of the leveraged-loan market this week that flatly disagree with each other. Today's briefing is about which one is telling the truth.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week this show has argued that the exit window is the binding constraint on this asset class. Distributions are frozen, the argument goes, because sellers cannot get out. The UK has just produced the one thing that argument has been missing. A real, competed, published clearing price.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power has SoftBank pricing a record one-trillion-yen retail bond, roughly six point three billion dollars, to fund its OpenAI commitments. That is a fixed coupon running through 2033, backing an equity stake with no market price, sold to Japanese retail households.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and the test I set myself. For three editions I said the August inflation prints were the calendar risk to my hawkish framing. Friday's consumer price report landed after that briefing went out. Core prices rose three tenths of a percent on the month, a tenth above most estimates.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — September 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Four days ago, three US agencies accused six Chinese labs of industrial-scale distillation against American models, and this show's complaint that day was that the advisory cited no telemetry sample, no forensic token log and no named source. This week the telemetry arrived.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 13, 2026
episodes.summary: On Friday this desk named the outcome that would hurt the most positions at once. A retracement in crude, we said, paired with an inflation print that wasn't hot enough to justify the pricing. The framing behind that call has been simple all week.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 13, 2026

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 13, 2026

Logic yields, then memory allocation, then packaging slots, then Nvidia's two hundred seventy-nine billion dollar memory prebuy. Friday broke that pattern.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 13, 2026

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — September 13, 2026
episodes.summary: This beat has spent the whole week on platforms selling optionality on unproven science. Today, look instead at where pharma is actually spending cash on AI, right now, before any clinical result exists.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 13, 2026
episodes.summary: This sector constantly asks you to grade a reservation as if it were a delivery. Today we can put both kinds of claim on the table side by side, and price the difference between them.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — September 13, 2026
episodes.summary: On Wednesday this briefing set itself a test. We said we could not tell which of two things the spread widening meant.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 13, 2026

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 13, 2026

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 13, 2026

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — September 14, 2026

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 14, 2026

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 14, 2026

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 14, 2026
episodes.summary: For five straight sessions this beat has had to discount the industry's biggest numbers. In every case the number was measured by the company that benefits from it.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 14, 2026

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 15, 2026

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 15, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the pattern this week. OpenAI is taking roughly one per-seat software category every week, and the tool doing the taking is not a better model. It's a connector.

episodes.summary: Here is what actually happened.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 15, 2026

Today's digital money read fills in the series.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — September 16, 2026
episodes.summary: The binary this show has tracked all week resolved yesterday afternoon, and it resolved against the industry. The Senate's cloture motion on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act failed, 49 to 50. Cloture needs 60. So this was not close.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 16, 2026
episodes.summary: For the past week this beat has kept returning to one argument. Announced capacity keeps losing to delivered capacity. And twice we guessed that some of the demand sitting in grid queues was speculative without being able to prove it. Today PJM's own market monitor put a number on that guess.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 16, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with memory, because memory is now the lead of this beat rather than a footnote to it. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix saw their finished-goods memory inventory fall below ten days of supply on September 7th. That is an unusually thin buffer.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 16, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the biggest AI product decisions weren't about who has the best model. They were about who gets distribution. And in each case a vendor traded something to get it — readiness for reach, or reach for control.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 16, 2026
episodes.summary: Let's start with a correction, because it matters more than the news it corrects.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 16, 2026
episodes.summary: Humanoid robotics is now running on two clocks, and yesterday both of them ticked. One clock reads a date eighteen months out. The other is a factory that has already cut its ribbon. Start with the date.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 16, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the sector's biggest claims moved further away from anything you can independently check. Meanwhile the one thing that actually happened in orbit was small, cheap, and Chinese.

episodes.summary: Apollo Global Management is in talks to buy Johnson and Johnson's DePuy Synthes orthopedics business. The reported price is close to twenty billion dollars. DePuy generated nine-point-three billion dollars in sales last year.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 16, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power has the first hard number behind an argument this beat has been making for weeks.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 16, 2026

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — September 17, 2026
episodes.summary: On Tuesday this beat said the Federal Reserve's decision was coming the next afternoon, and that nothing about the outcome was settled. It is settled now. It went the other way.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 17, 2026
episodes.summary: For six straight sessions, this beat has had to discount nearly every big number in the industry, because the party quoting it was also the party who benefits from it.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 17, 2026
episodes.summary: On Sunday, this briefing priced production voice agents at five cents a minute and called that telephony economics rather than token economics. Two days later, that anchor broke. Google published rates a fraction of it. Let's start there.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — September 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Let's start with Salesforce's own numbers, because they answer a question this beat has been chasing all week. On September 16th, Salesforce published its second Agentic Enterprise Index.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 17, 2026

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with a correction this show owes you. Three days ago we walked through SpaceX's pre-listing financials. We flagged Starlink's roughly 39 percent operating margin as an artifact of launch priced internally.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — September 17, 2026

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — September 17, 2026

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 18, 2026

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — September 18, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop, and with Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar, because everything else on today's tape traces back to it.

This beat called Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the line that carries crude across the kingdom to Yanbu on the Red Sea, bypassing Hormuz, the kingdom's single remaining point of failure. episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — September 19, 2026

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: This week, the product news stopped being about which assistant you talk to. It became about who owns the corpus underneath the assistant, and where the meter sits behind the flat-rate plan. We start with the corpus.

episodes.summary: The most useful number in enterprise AI this month did not come from a keynote. It came from an invoice. On September 1st, GitHub's promotional Copilot credits expired. The included usage per seat dropped, and the seat price stayed exactly where it was.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: Humanoid vendors will not publish a fielded-reliability number. No intervention rate, no uptime, no cost per completed task. This week a number arrived anyway, and it came from outside the vendors entirely. It came as a share price, and it went down.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — September 19, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the thing to watch was not a launch. It was a contract structure. The US government is buying an outcome instead of a satellite count, and that changes where value accrues in orbit.

episodes.summary: The most useful thing that happened this week is a sale where the money came from outside private equity. H.I.G.
